page: Amazon Web Services m8in.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, with 2 threads enabled per core. The instance provides 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware connectivity is characterized by a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, providing substantial network throughput capacity. The instance includes no integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent and operational disk volumes must be provisioned via networked block storage like Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). It also features no discrete graphical processing units (GPUs) and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The qualitative profile of the m8in.16xlarge presents a balanced compute-to-memory configuration combined with high-speed networking capabilities. This profile delivers strong resource density for distributed enterprise services without the operational overhead of managing physical hosts. However, the reliance entirely on remote storage introduces an external latency dependency for disk-bound operations compared to configurations offering direct-attached NVMe storage.

Given its hardware specifications and 100 Gbps network baseline, the m8in.16xlarge is suited for network-intensive enterprise workloads. Key target applications include large-scale distributed caching layers, inter-service microservice backbones, multi-node application servers, relational database clusters backed by network storage, and continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines requiring high cross-node data transfer.

It provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores, accompanied by 256.0 GB of RAM at an even 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Designed for network-demanding environments, the instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It contains no onboard local storage, depending entirely on network-attached storage architectures, and does not include GPU acceleration hardware. The balance of 64 vCPUs, 256.0 GB of memory, and high network throughput makes this instance appropriate for multi-tier enterprise workloads, high-throughput web serving, container orchestration nodes, distributed relational database systems, and clustered data processing tasks requiring fast inter-node communication.
